# DarkSlide v1.2.4

DarkSlide 1.2.4 brings in the most useful ideas from Durieux's ([@tdurieux](https://github.com/tdurieux)) [DarkSlide fork](https://github.com/tdurieux/DarkSlide), adapted to 1.2.3's editor and conversion pipeline. It makes full-roll work faster and crops more dependable, and adds tooling to measure color accuracy. Conversion color output is unchanged from 1.2.3.

## Highlights

- **Auto crop finds the image gate more reliably.** Portrait scans, film rebates, sprocket holes on one or both edges, and square (126, 6×6) or medium-format gates are recognized. Format guards only ever expand a crop toward a plausible film aspect; they never trim image area.
- **Crops land in the right place on rotated scans.** Rotating a cropped image by 90° previously moved the crop to the wrong area, and auto crop placed its frame incorrectly on EXIF-rotated scans. Both now follow the image. The detected tilt is no longer applied automatically; a manual level angle is kept, and the crop is fitted inside it. The same fixes apply to batch export.
- **Stabilize Crops for a whole roll.** A new action on the roll card detects every frame, shares a robust (median) crop size between frames scanned at the same size, and keeps each frame's own position. Scans of different sizes or orientations never share a crop. Frames with manual crops are left alone unless you choose to include them, and each changed frame can be undone.
- **Better crop and straighten controls.** Edge as well as corner handles, Shift to keep the current ratio, pen and touch support, arrow-key nudging, and click-to-reposition. Draw a line along a horizon or vertical edge to level the photo. Crops that already match a preset ratio highlight it, and the crop pane shows the current size and ratio.
- **Fine adjustment buttons.** −/+ steppers on Exposure, Contrast, Black and White Point, Saturation, Temperature, Tint, the RGB balance sliders, and Level. Each click is one undo step.
- **A more informative histogram.** Channel toggles, luminance P1/median/P99, and shadow and highlight clipping warnings measured per RGB channel, so a saturated color that clips one channel is flagged even when luminance is not. A labelled LOG toggle switches to a logarithmic height scale.
- **Zoom that follows the cursor.** Wheel and pinch zoom start from the fitted view instead of jumping to 100%, keep the point under the cursor in place, and scale smoothly with trackpad deltas. Very large scans can zoom out to their fit scale below 10%.
- **Faster RAW handoff.** Decoded RAW pixels now travel from the native decoder as compact binary data instead of a JSON array of numbers, and decoding runs off the app's main thread with at most two RAW developments at once. The samples are bit-identical; RAW development is unchanged.
- **Lower memory for batch selections.** Opening several scans or a folder for batch export no longer reads every file into memory first; each file is read when the batch reaches it.
- **Preview rendering cancels the right job.** When a new edit supersedes a running preview for another document, the running preview is now cancelled instead of the incoming one, and a failed render no longer stalls newer queued work.
- **Color-accuracy evaluator (developer tooling).** `npm run evaluate:color` compares exported 8-bit sRGB TIFFs of measured charts with D50 Lab references and reports CIEDE2000 statistics. It rejects inputs it would measure under the wrong color assumptions and requires full capture provenance. No accuracy claim is made from the tool itself; see [`evaluation/README.md`](https://github.com/kilianvivien/DarkSlide/blob/main/evaluation/README.md).

## Not included

These fork ideas were reviewed and deferred because they change the conversion output or the preview lifecycle and need real-scan measurements first: the on-disk RAW preview cache and reduced-resolution RAW previews, camera white balance for RAW, automatic tone redesign, lens-distortion correction, concurrent batch workers, instant CSS preview approximations, background (non-activating) multi-file imports, high-resolution zoom regions, and the full editor redesign.

## Desktop Downloads

GitHub Actions builds and attaches installers for each supported desktop platform:

- macOS: universal Apple Silicon and Intel `.dmg`
- Windows: `.msi` and NSIS `.exe`
- Linux: `.deb` and `.AppImage`

## Installation Notes

- macOS builds are not notarized. On first launch, macOS may require opening the app through System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
- Windows and Linux builds are unsigned.

## Validation

Type-checking, ESLint, all 793 tests across 61 test files, the production web build, and the Rust tests passed. New coverage includes render-queue cancellation, crop geometry checked against the worker's actual rotation transform, frame detection on synthetic and real 126 film, roll stabilization and undo, step-button undo entries, histogram clipping, cursor-anchored zoom, binary RAW payload validation, and the 34 published CIEDE2000 reference pairs. The test suites that previously depended on a non-redistributable LUT file now use a generated fixture and run everywhere.
